subject: Biotechnology
title: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy
description: A 60-second lesson on Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy.

hook.text: Three-parent babies — mitochondrial replacement therapy prevents devastating diseases by combining DNA from three people.

buildup.text: Mitochondrial diseases affect 1 in 5,000 births — faulty mitochondria cause seizures, blindness, heart failure, and early death.

discovery.text: MRT swaps faulty mitochondria for healthy ones — the child has nuclear DNA from two parents and mitochondrial DNA from a donor.

twist.text: The UK legalized MRT in 2015 — the first country to approve a form of heritable human genetic modification.

climax.text: The first MRT baby was born in 2016 — but carried only 1% donor mitochondria, raising questions about long-term effectiveness.

punchline.text: Three genetic parents, one healthy child — MRT blurs boundaries while preventing tragedy.

quiz.question: Why is mitochondrial replacement therapy considered a form of heritable genetic modification?
options: It changes the child's nuclear DNA permanently
The donor mitochondrial DNA is passed to all future generations through the maternal line
It creates a genetically identical copy of the donor
